10800.author: fwyzard
10800.body:
Prevent a deadlock between `hipEventSynchronize` and `hipMallocAsync`.

`hipMallocAsync` may try to acquire the device lock while it holds the memory pool lock, if the pool needs to allocate more memory.

`hipEventSynchronize` will try to acquire the memory pool lock while holding the device lock, to free the unused memory in the pool.

This may cause a deadlock if the two operations happen on different threads at the same time.

This change makes `MemoryPool::ReleaseFreedMemory` (called by `hipEventSynchronize`) return immediately if it cannot acquire the pool lock.

We also build `libamdhip64.so` with debug symbols.
10800.title: Prevent a deadlock in ROCm

51413.body:
On top of https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/45216 to check in a real-life workflow that it works. 

Migrate the double/vdouble reconstruction parameters in RecoHGCal/TICL and in the HGCAL layer-clustering algorithms (RecoLocalCalo/HGCalRecProducers, both the legacy CPU HGCalCLUEAlgo/HGCalLayerClusterProducer and the Alpaka SoA producers) to float/vfloat, and update the corresponding offline and Phase-2 HLT configurations.

Many reco parameters are cut thresholds, angular/geometric windows, working points and per-layer weights carrying at most a few significant figures, and they are compared against data that is already stored as float (layer clusters, tracksters, SoA columns). Storing them as float aligns the parameter type with the data, removes redundant double->float narrowing at the read sites, and is a first step toward propagating float precision through the reco chain.
51413.title: move HGCAL configuration parameters from double to float

51526.author: namapane
51526.body:
This PR includes a number of updates, clean-ups and minor improvements of the MF subsystems aimed at long-term maintenance and future development.

1. Uniformize the creation of interpolators between the DDD and DD4Hep geometry builders. Besides removing some code duplication, this enables both versions to read merged tables instead than one individual table for each volume, and opens the possibility of distributing only the merged tables in [cms-data/MagneticField-Interpolation](https://github.com/cms-data/MagneticField-Interpolation), dropping the individual tables. (Note: the DDD version is deprecated, but cannot be removed until the whole DDD support is dropped, starting from [here](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/Configuration/StandardSequences/python/MagneticField_cff.py). It also turns out that the TEve-based MF visualiaztion only works with the DDD builder since it relies on TGeoMgrFromDdd, and no equivalent exists for DD4hep, to my knowledge).
Also, added the possibility to read tables for an absolute path, which can be useful for special studies (recent use case: special sets of tables for model version 170812 Run I, Run II, and MTCC-like conditions made available for comparison to proponents of the Z mass analysis on  `/eos/cms/store/group/alca_magfield/CMSSW/`)
1. Release the scripts to convert tables for the "final" MF model, version 170812, that can be released in the future.
1. Put some order in the different places where the MF XML geometry was defined, using standardized cff files. 
1. Handle an extremely rare case of numerical accuracy at the barrel-endcap boundary. Although this has practically zero impact on tracking (it was never noticed), it is better to solve it.
1.  Use the correct values for nominal magnet currents everywhere. The values currently in the code are a bit larger than in reality (e.g. 18268 instead of 18164). This derives from a misunderstanding at the time of MTCC: the currents used as input for early FEM models were tuned in an attempt to reproduce the central field strength, and for some reason these values were picked instead of the actual currents. (Subsequent improvements of the model result in excellent agreement with no need to tweak the currents). This fix has no effect on results since the values of nominal currents are only used to pick the map corresponding to the nominal working point, so the precise value that is used does not matter (i.e.: a current of 18000 or 18200 A equally gives the map for the nominal 3.8 T conditions). However, these shifted values in the code can cause some confusion among users (received some inquiries on this recently).

#### PR validation:
- repeated all validation steps indicated in the [MF documentation](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/SWGuideMagneticField?redirectedfrom=CMS.SWGuideMagneticField#Development_workflow)
- standard regression vs pre-computed values succeeds
- ad-hoc tests reading merged tables with the DDD builder, and of reading tables from absolute paths.
51526.title: Updates and maintenance of the MagneticField subsystem

51593.author: fnenna
51593.body:
#### PR description: The goal of this PR is to optimize tracker muon reconstruction in the ME0 station ($2.0 < |\eta| < 2.8$). The ME0 station is characterized by fine segmentation in the $\phi$ direction and coarse segmentation in $\eta$. The standard arbitration procedure to find the best track-segment matching relies on $\Delta R = \sqrt{(\Delta X)^2 + (\Delta Y)^2}$; however, this approach limits efficiency for tracker muons in ME0 due to the limited precision of the $\Delta Y$ information. To address this, the strategy introduced in this PR refines the track-segment matching selection through: * A loose cut on $\Delta Y$, ensuring that matched tracks and segments belong to the same $\eta$ partition or adjacent ones. * A discrimination metric that selects the closest pairs based on the two most precise observables provided by ME0 chambers: $$\mathrm{Metric} = \left(\frac{\Delta X}{\sigma_{\Delta X}}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\Delta(d\phi/dz)}{\sigma_{\Delta(d\phi/dz)}}\right)^2$$ This new strategy results in an increased average reconstruction efficiency and significantly improves its uniformity across the entire ME0 acceptance [1]. The full study is documented [here](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1638450/#15-phase-2-studies-with-me0-re). Additional Details * Since the ME0 segment reconstruction algorithm uses $X$ coordinates, $d\phi/dz$ is computed using the furthest hits of the segment within the station. * Two normalization factors, derived from distributions in the no-PU scenario [2], are introduced to make the two components of the discrimination metric comparable. [1]

[2]

#### PR description:

PR addresses issue https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/48499. The pixel template-related code has many interpolation calculations in the form of `(1-r)*a + r*b`. Compiler uses fused multiply-add, but it has the freedom to choose which term to multiply first. A logically transparent change to the code can then cause small numerical differences depending if it causes the compiler to choose differently in some of the interpolation calculations (explained in [this comment](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/48499#issuecomment-3110295572)). The PR introduces interpolate 1D / 2D methods that specifically call `std::fma` to resolve the ambiguity.

Many small changes are expected in test workflows, but any additional innocuous changes to the code should no longer report many differences.

51637.author: EmanueleCoradin
51637.body:
#### PR description:

This PR proposes a solution to the overflow reported in issue #51614 when running batched `PyTorchAlpaka` inference in `testPyTorchAlpakaTestSerialSync`.

For a batched tensor, `TensorCollection` advances the input pointer to the beginning of the selected batch. However, `TensorHandle` previously instructed `Policy` to copy the full tensor storage extent, as if the pointer still referred to the beginning of the SoA memory block.

When the pointer was shifted to a later batch, this caused the copy to extend past the end of the original allocation. The additional copied elements were outside the storage span addressed by the PyTorch tensor, so the inference results remained correct despite the invalid read.

This PR introduces `num_spanned_elements()`, which computes the correct contiguous memory span required by the tensor. The calculated extent is then passed to `Policy`, preventing the out-of-bounds copy.
51637.title: Fix PyTorchAlpaka Policy

51733.author: mmusich
51733.body:
#### PR description:

Adds a generic, templated DQM source (`GenericObjectDQMSource<T>`) that books and fills one 1D histogram per data member of an EDM object type `T`, driven by a per-type trait specialization (`DQMVariableTraits<T>`) rather than a hand-written analyzer per collection type.

In the package `DQMServices/Components`:

- `interface/DQMVariable.h`: descriptor for a scalar member (name, title, binning, accessor)
- `interface/DQMVectorVariable.h`: descriptor for a vector-valued member (e.g. per-track or per-crystal quantities); filled once per element per event
- `interface/GenericObjectDQMSource.h`: the templated `DQMEDAnalyzer` itself; detects at compile time (via `if constexpr`) whether a given `DQMVariableTraits<T>` specialization also provides `vectorVariables()`, so scalar-only types are unaffected by the vector-variable support.

Trait specializations and one-line plugin registrations for:
- `reco::Track`
- `reco::Muon`
- `Run3ScoutingTrack`
- `Run3ScoutingElectron` (including per-track vector members)
- `Run3ScoutingPhoton` (including per-crystal energy/timing/detId matrices)

Extending to a new object type requires only a new `DQMVariableTraits<T>` specialization and a ~5-line plugin .cc file; `GenericObjectDQMSource` itself does not change.

#### PR validation:

Compiled against the current IB. Ran each new DQM source standalone over a representative dataset/relval for its input collection with cmsRun, confirmed the expected histograms are booked under the configured DQM folder with no MonitorElement booking errors, and visually inspected the output ROOT/DQM GUI file to confirm distributions are non-empty and binning is sane. No existing modules or output are modified by this PR,  it only adds new, opt-in plugins.
Example configuration:

```python
process.run3ScoutingTrackGenericDQMSource = cms.EDProducer(
    "Run3ScoutingTrackGenericDQMSource",
    src = cms.InputTag("hltScoutingTrackPacker"),
    folder = cms.string("Scouting/GenericTrack"),
)

process.run3ScoutingPhotonGenericDQMSource = cms.EDProducer(
    "Run3ScoutingPhotonGenericDQMSource",
    src = cms.InputTag("hltScoutingEgammaPacker"),
    folder = cms.string("Scouting/GenericPhoton"),
)
process.run3ScoutingElectronGenericDQMSource = cms.EDProducer(
    "Run3ScoutingElectronGenericDQMSource",
    src = cms.InputTag("hltScoutingEgammaPacker"),
    folder = cms.string("Scouting/GenericElectron"),
```

51744.body:
#### PR description:
major update of the Phase2TrackerDigitizer package to address the high CPU usage
 - all the SimHits are processed in a single loop sequentially. A std::set which was keeping track of unique detIDs and a std::vector which was collecting SimHits for a particular DetId using std::copy_if() are dropped

  - std::map::emplace() replaced   std::map::try_emplace()  wherever applicable
  - std::vector::push_back() replaced with std::emplace_back() wherever applicable
  - variable/function names updated to make more meaningful 
  - C++17 standard implemented 
  - some code cleanup

51754.author: AuroraPerego
51754.body:
#### PR description:

This PR modifies the logic used in CLUE3D to create tracksters in the barrel. The goal is to avoid having multiple ECAL clusters in the same 3D trackster, as linking them is the job of the superclustering step that will happen later.
The code is entirely in the `isBarrel_` check, so it should not affect the endcap, and it splits tracksters whenever an ECAL cluster is going to be attached to a trackster that already contains one. If one of the two is the seed, the other is removed and creates a new trackster on its own. If neither of them is the seed, only the closest one to the seed is kept.

#### PR validation:

Tested on wf 31953.209, checking that with this PR there are no CLUE3D tracksters with more than one ECAL cluster in the barrel.

FYI @valsdav
51754.title: Modify CLUE3D in the barrel for EGM linking
